title: ID-JAG Runner: cross-app access against a real PingFederate

glossary.definition: Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant. PingFederate issues a short-lived signed JWT assertion that a second authorization server can redeem for tokens, so a client never hands its own user tokens across app boundaries.
RFC 8693. A client sends one token and gets a different one back, for example an ID-JAG assertion in exchange for the user's ID token, refresh token or access token.
RFC 7523. The client proves who it is by presenting a signed JWT assertion instead of a shared secret; the resource-AS validates the signature, issuer, audience and expiry.

grant_type=password (RFC 6749 section 4.3). The client sends the user's username and password straight to the token endpoint. Legacy, but useful in a lab to get a real token set without a browser sign-in.
RFC 7662. A resource server asks the authorization server whether a token is active and what it allows, using its own client credentials.

The negative tests that prove the grant is real: a wrong client cannot redeem the assertion, a wrong resource is refused as invalid_target, a forged assertion fails signature validation, and a wrong scope is denied.
Client secrets typed into the lab are held in server memory for the session only, never echoed in any response, trace or log, and never stored.
The lab's outbound guard: it allows calls to the one PingFederate runtime configured in Settings and refuses everything else before a socket opens.

sources.title: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693)
sources.use: Background for the ID-JAG exchange card.

cards.label: Start the lab and check it
cards.description: npm install && npm start (or docker compose up). The lab binds loopback only; health is demo-health/1.

cards.label: Point the lab at a PingFederate 13.1+
cards.description: Any https origin works (a default demo runtime ships configured). The idjag-* demo objects must exist on the target PingFederate.

cards.label: Get a real token set (password grant, then refresh)
cards.description: Act 1 posts grant_type=password, then a refresh grant that returns the ID token. Every hop shows its redacted wire trace.

cards.label: Exchange for an ID-JAG
cards.description: Act 2 runs RFC 8693 token exchange for the ID-JAG token type with three subject variants: ID token, refresh token, access token. The assertion's header and claims are decoded and shown.

cards.label: Redeem the assertion at the resource AS
cards.description: Act 3 redeems the ID-JAG with a jwt-bearer grant at the resource-AS client, then introspects the resulting token with a third client.

cards.label: Prove the refusals
cards.description: Act 4 runs the four refusal cases: unauthorized_client, invalid_target, a forged assertion, and a wrong scope. Each refusal shows the real PingFederate error.

cards.label: Why the secrets never come back
cards.description: Client secrets are typed per session and write-only: never returned by any API, redacted in every trace.
